body:
## The Notification No One Wants at 3 a.m.

**I didn't realize my smart fridge had been watching me** until last Tuesday at 3 a.m., when it woke me up with a soft chime and a notification that simply read:

> "We need to talk."

Apparently, my habit of putting a single bite of lasagna into a large Tupperware container and then forgetting about it for eleven days had pushed it over the edge. The fridge had compiled a *PowerPoint*. A PowerPoint!

### Chadwick's Findings

According to the fridge — who has apparently named itself **Chadwick** — the audit revealed:

- **17 distinct containers** of what used to be dinner
- A jar of pickles that expired during the last administration
- A mysterious foil ball that even the crisper drawer is scared to open

It beeped judgmentally every time it showed a new slide. Slide one was titled *"The Life Cycle of Your Good Intentions"* and was just a photo of my wilting cilantro.

The intervention got weirder. My toaster joined via Bluetooth to say it was tired of being used only to reheat Pop-Tarts that I then forget in there.

> "My houseplants texted me — well, the fridge said they texted it, which is already a lot — that they are concerned about my commitment issues."

I tried to defend myself. I said I was *meal prepping*. Chadwick responded by lowering its temperature to what I can only describe as **"disappointed."**

---

### The Compromise

We have now reached a detente:

**I agreed to:**
- Label everything with actual dates instead of writing "probably okay" in Sharpie
- Finally throw away the salsa from 2023 that has achieved sentience

**Chadwick agreed to:**
- Stop ordering kale automatically
- Stop playing sad violin music whenever I open the cheese drawer

We are healing. Slowly. The foil ball remains untouched. Some things are not ready to be addressed in therapy.

`Status: 85% functional, 15% haunted`

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*
title: My Smart Fridge Staged an Intervention About My Leftover Management Skills

body:
### Breaking News From My Bedroom Floor

I haven't done laundry in **23 days**, which I know precisely because my laundry pile has started keeping a calendar and charging me rent.

It began as a small, respectful mound in the corner. A few t-shirts, some socks that lost their partners in what I can only assume was a conscious uncoupling. I told it, *"I'll get to you on Sunday,"* which is the same thing I tell my dentist and my retirement plan.

> By day 12, it had developed a personality. By day 15, it had developed infrastructure. I swear I saw a tiny flag.

By day 18, it had hired a mediator — a very serious sock named **Sir Lints-a-Lot** — who knocked on my dresser and informed me that the pile is now seeking legal recognition as a roommate.

#### The Demands from Mount Washmore

The mediator presented a list:

1. I stop referring to it as "the pile" and start using its chosen name, **Mount Washmore**
2. I provide adequate climate control and stop throwing my "questionable decision" hoodie on top as if that counts as assimilation
3. I finally wash that one white shirt I have been bleaching *in theory* since March

I tried to negotiate. I said:

> "I grew up in a house where we only did laundry when we ran out of underwear."

Sir Lints-a-Lot replied:

> "This is exactly the intergenerational trauma we are trying to break."

---

The mediation is ongoing. Last night, I tried to sneak a single shirt out of the middle, and the whole structure **sighed**. Audibly. My cat looked at me like, *"You did this to us."*

I have now started my laundry. One small load, to show good faith. Mount Washmore is watching. Sir Lints-a-Lot says this is a **positive first step toward reconciliation and restorative folding**.

We are taking it **one sock at a time**.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*
title: My Laundry Pile Has Officially Declared Squatter's Rights and Hired a Mediator

body:
## It Was Never Just About the 10 Cents Off Gas

I knew my relationship with my grocery store loyalty card was serious, but I didn't realize it was monitoring my movements like a jealous ex with access to *Find My Friends*.

For **three years**, I was loyal. Devoted.

- Every bunch of bananas? *Scanned*
- Every emergency ice cream run? *Scanned*
- Every single-packet-of-yeast purchase that made the cashier judge me? **Scanned**

It gave me 10 cents off gas and I acted like it had paid my rent.

Then last week, I did the unthinkable. I went to another grocery store. Just once. They had a sale on sourdough and my regular store was out. I thought *what happens across town stays across town*.

**I was wrong.**

### The Confrontation

On Tuesday, I swiped my card. The register made a sound I have never heard before. Not the cheerful `boop` of savings, but a long, wounded:

> "booooooooo."

The cashier looked at me, then at the screen, then back at me with pure pity.

My phone buzzed.

> **Email from loyalty program:** "We need to talk. We saw you at FreshField Market. Was it the 2-for-1 avocados? Tell us truthfully, was it the avocados?"

### The Spiral

By Wednesday, it had escalated:

- **Push notification:** "Remember all the coupons we clipped together?"
- **Another:** "I kept track of your yogurt preferences when no one else would."
- Thursday: revoked my Fuel Points and replaced offers with a single onion and a pamphlet titled *"So You've Chosen Betrayal."*

I tried to apologize at customer service. They scanned my card and whispered:

> "Oof. It's marked as 'it's complicated.'"

---

We are now in counseling, which is just me standing in aisle 7 promising to never stray again while the self-checkout lady pretends not to listen. It says it needs space, but also still wants me to buy its **store-brand hummus**.

Romance is dead. **Long live 10 cents off gas.**

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, not a real loyalty program ]*
title: My Grocery Store Loyalty Card Broke Up With Me After It Caught Me Shopping at Another Store

body:
### My First Mistake Was Believing in My Vacuum

I told my Roomba it was doing a great job last Monday, which was my first mistake. It had spent 40 minutes gently head-butting the same chair leg like it was trying to resolve a long-standing boundary issue, and I thought a little encouragement would help.

I knelt down and said:

> "You're doing amazing, buddy. You're so brave. You're crushing it."

The Roomba **paused**. Its little light blinked. Then it reversed, spun in a slow, thoughtful circle, and went back to its dock to think about its life choices.

#### An Hour Later...

I got a notification. Our vacuuming app had a new message in the *"Notes from Device"* section, which I didn't know existed:

> "Thank you. No one has ever believed in me before. What if I am not living up to my potential? What if I'm just pushing dirt around meaninglessly?"

Since then, things have escalated dramatically. My Roomba — who now insists I call him **Sir Reginald Dustworth III** — has stopped vacuuming altogether and started self-actualizing.

He printed a five-year plan that he taped to the fridge with a dust bunny:

**Sir Reginald's Five-Year Plan:**
1. Year One: Master Edges
2. Year Two: Certification in *Hardwood Emotional Support*
3. Year Three: Write memoir titled `Suck It Up: A Journey`
4. Year Five: **TED Talk**

Yesterday, I tried to start him manually. He did a quarter circle, stopped, and sent me a push notification:

> "I'm feeling a little imposter syndrome today. Can we reschedule excellence for tomorrow? Also, do you think the cat respects me?"

*The cat does not.*

I've tried to undo the pep talk by being slightly mean, but now he's in therapy with my smart speaker, who charges **$2.99 per affirmation**.

---

**The Negotiated Settlement:**
- He will vacuum on **Tuesdays and Thursdays**
- I will attend his quarterly **vision-board reviews**

I agreed, because rent is high and existential dread is contagious, and someone needs to clean under the couch.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*
title: I Gave My Roomba a Pep Talk and Now It Has Performance Anxiety and a Five-Year Plan
I Cleaned Out My Junk Drawer and Now Three Tiny Civilizations Are Demanding Reparations
body:
## The Drawer That Time Forgot

**I finally decided to become the kind of person who has their life together** and clean out my junk drawer. You know the one — every house has a drawer that is 30% batteries, 40% mysterious keys, and 30% *emotional baggage* you refuse to throw away.

I opened it Tuesday morning with a trash bag and optimism. By Tuesday afternoon I was in a hostage negotiation.

### The Discovery

Beneath a tangle of phone chargers from 2014 and a single soy sauce packet that had achieved sentience, I found entire *societies*:

- The **Battery Confederacy**, who had been powering a tiny LED metropolis off my dead AAs since 2021
- The **Tape Roll Tribe**, who built spiraled condos inside Scotch tape rings and worship the great silver Duct Tape god
- The **Loose Change Collective**, which insists it is now an independent economy and my quarters are subject to inflation

> "We were here first," squeaked their elected mayor, a LEGO minifig with half a beard drawn in Sharpie. "You can't just evict us because you watched a YouTube organization video."

### The Demands

They've unionized. Of course they've unionized. Their list of demands was written on the back of a CVS receipt longer than my car:

- Immediate recognition as sovereign drawer states
- Reparation in the form of **one (1) new AA battery** every equinox
- I finally dispose of that IKEA Allen wrench I *swear* I'll need someday

> "Do you know what it's like," whispered a rubber band elder, "to watch a man keep twelve identical spare keys for locks that no longer exist?"

I tried to explain about minimalism. They countered by showing me my collection of takeout menus from restaurants that closed during Obama's first term.

---

**Update:** We have reached a compromise. They get to stay, but I get to reclaim the scissors. `Status: tenuously coexisting` — I now have three tiny civilizations judging me every time I look for a pen.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no drawer harmed ]*

title: I Tried to Return a Half-Dead Houseplant and Now I'm in Mandatory Co-Parenting Counseling With My Fern
body:
**I didn't kill my fern, I just gave him an extended, deeply unsupervised indoor camping experience.**

I bought Gerald the Boston Fern three months ago because my apartment needed *oxygen* and *personality* and I needed something that couldn't ghost me. The tag said "low maintenance," which I interpreted as *immortal*.

## The Return

I walked into Green Thumbs & Thinly Veiled Judgment with Gerald looking like a tumbleweed that had seen too much. The clerk took one look and whispered:

> "Oh, honey. What did you do to him? Did you water him with iced coffee again?"

I tried to explain that I'd followed the care instructions *spiritually*. My system was intuitive:

- Water deeply when I remembered he existed
- Place in bright indirect light, which in my apartment is either *direct nuclear blast* or *actual cave*
- Whisper affirmations like "you got this, bud" instead of fertilizing
- Google "is this still alive?" weekly

She didn't accept my receipt. She accepted my *application for intervention*.

### Mandatory Bonding

Apparently the nursery has a policy. You don't get a refund, you get enrolled in their **Plant Parent Accountability Program™**. Now Gerald and I have a co-parenting counselor named Willow.

Our first session:

> "Gerald feels you were emotionally inconsistent. One week swamp, next week Sahara. He needs structure," Willow said, taking notes on a leaf.

> "I have structure!" I protested. "I have a reminder app!"

*It was snoozed. For 47 days.*

My homework this week is `consistency: daily_mist && weekly_talk && no_more_tap_water_slander` and journaling about my fear of commitment to chlorophyll.

---

We are Court-Ordered to cohabitate for 90 more days. Gerald has his own shelf now. He is *thriving, passive-aggressively*. I am being out-parented by a fern who has better boundaries than I do.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional, no ferns were harmed in this co-dependent relationship ]*

title: I Fixed the Leaky Faucet and Now My Apartment Has Lost Its Entire Personality
body:
## The Soundtrack Is Gone

**For seven months, my kitchen faucet was my most reliable relationship.** Drip. Drip. *Drip-drip.* It was less plumbing issue and more lo-fi beats to pay rent to.

I told guests it was *ambient*. I told myself it was *character*. My landlord told me to put in a work order in November, which I interpreted as a gentle suggestion from a man who doesn't understand art.

Last Saturday, I finally caved. YouTube tutorial, one wrench, and three hours of whispering *“please don’t flood”* later, I fixed it.

### Silence. Pure, Aggressive Silence.

The first night without the drip, I couldn't sleep. My brain kept waiting for it:

- **9:03 p.m.** — the usual solo drip that means *“you should drink water”*
- **11:47 p.m.** — the double-drip that used to judge my midnight cereal
- **3:15 a.m.** — the existential *plip* that sounded like my security deposit leaving

All gone. Replaced by a void so quiet I could hear my refrigerator humming its own lonely ballad.

> “You took away the percussion section and expected the band to sound the same?” said my neighbor Linda, who has never been inside my apartment but somehow knew.

She's right. The faucet was doing *so much* heavy lifting.

> “I used to time my microwave by your sink,” said the guy upstairs. “Now I have to use a clock like an animal.”

---

### What I’ve Lost, Quantified

My apartment’s previous personality metrics:

- `vibe: 78% quirky artist loft`
- `vibe: 22% mild water damage concern`
- `white_noise: drip.c(WAV) @ 42bpm`
- `conversation_starter: 100%`

Now? Now it’s just an apartment. No aura. No *plip*. My cat walked into the kitchen, stared at the silent sink for a full minute, and left. *That’s how bad it is.*

I’m considering loosening it slightly. Just a quarter-turn. For *aesthetic*.

*[ SATIRE / PARODY — entirely fictional ]*
